notes: Entries with kind 'value' change the number (and possibly conf); kind 'conf' changes only the confidence; kind 'basis' keeps value and conf but replaces a basis that misquotes, misattributes or cites the wrong source (from == to). changes.basis: X post, 14 Sep 2026: progress 'should be slower than it otherwise could be… Pacing will be well worth this cost'. Pacing, not a multi-year delay.
X, 14 Sep 2026: 'When we talk about pacing, we do not mean stopping', but progress 'should be slower than it otherwise could be'. Also: 'we need to pace the frontier'.
2025 Senate: the US lead over China is 'not a huge amount of time'. But Sept 2026: 'no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness'. No verbatim 'keep pushing'.
Davos, Jan 2026: 'good to have a slightly slower pace… so that we can get this right societally'. On Amodei's slow-down essay (X, 12 Sep 2026): 'the direction is correct'.
On 'We must slow the pace' (X, 12 Sep 2026): 'points towards the right path forward… the direction is correct'. July 2026: safe only 'if we give ourselves the time and space'.
Asked at Davos 2026 whether he would back a pause if every company and country joined: 'I think so', given 'international collaboration'. Still building AGI; no decades-long halt.
Jan 2026: stopping is 'fundamentally untenable'. Sept 2026: 'Pacing does not mean halting' — yet on an intergovernmental 'pause': 'I support floating this', though 'unlikely'.
Against any pause, but superalignment 'very well may require us to slow down at some critical moments'; a healthy lead lets the US 'cash in' part of it 'to get safety right'.
Plan A (co-author) is a bilateral US–China 'brake pedal'. The go-it-alone pacing argument comes from an AI Futures post he did not write (thanked for feedback only).
Takeover is 'preposterous' (TIME 2024); p(doom) numbers are 'pulled out of thin air' — but 'I didn't say p(doom) was zero' (X, 21 Apr 2026). Do not quote him as saying 'zero'.
No statement on the trade-off itself. Stance implied: takeover 'preposterous', and on Amodei's call to slow down: 'Everyone should make fun of them now' (Sept 2026).
'The options are to grow or die'; 'I'm not trying to actually replace humans', yet e/acc is 'not just centred on humanity'. Optimism is about growth; 'maximal growth' is not in the source.
The cited quote is about hype selling products, not about states. Closest: the race is 'not a preordained path where our only choice is how fast to run' (DAIR statement, 2023).
No statement of hers on the lives-saved trade-off in the sources opened; inferred from 'distracts from the real harms that are happening now' and the book's anti-hype thesis.
Inferred from a ~70% default-path catastrophe estimate known here only via a third-party summary; no statement of his on a 1% threshold 'whatever the benefits'.
On keeping humans 'dominant' over 'submissive' AI: 'That's not going to work. They're going to be much smarter than us' (Ai4 conference, Aug 2025).
Amodei's call to slow down is 'very sensible'; until control is solved 'it would be foolish to develop' superintelligent AI (ABC, 14 Sep 2026).
Co-author, 'Managing extreme AI risks' (Science, 2024): 'Governments must be prepared to license their development'. The cited Senate blog post never says 'licence'.
'Shut it all down… no exceptions'; even a careful lab's restraint only means a careless one 'destroy[s] the world two years later' (AGI Ruin). Semafor's 'should shut down' is a paraphrase.
'I don't think stagnation or slowing down is actually an option' (Lex Fridman #407); e/acc: 'You cannot stop the acceleration.'
Plan A (co-author): the US and China 'delay the creation of superintelligence to 2040'; without the deal it arrives in 2030. A decade's delay, as a recommendation.
Plan A Phase 1: 'temporarily pause training', then 'resume R&D under safety-case regulation' — builders must make the safety case. (The 'risk threshold' quote is his colleagues'.)
Plan A: 'Track where all the compute is'; R&D resumes only 'under safety-case regulation'. The detailed pacing menu is an AI Futures post he did not author.
'Any arms control equilibrium… seems extremely unstable. In short, "breakout" is too easy'; an international treaty on safety 'seems fanciful to me'.
